report.source_text: Intraoperatively the patient was kept on left side 20° with an incision done in the right nostril, the mucosa was separated and the sphenoid sinus mucosa removed. The sellar floor identified and removed. Thick capsule of abscess incised with yellowish pus was drained. The cavity was cleaned and irrigated with antibiotics and saline. The pus was sent for Gram stain, culture, acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stain and histopathological evaluation. The pituitary was not removed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old man presented with a month-long history of severe headache, photosensitivity, nausea, left eye blurred vision, generalized fatigue, loss of libido, erectile dysfunction, polyuria, and polydipsia. MRI of the brain revealed a heterogeneously hyperintense lesion on T2-weighted images with peripheral hypointensity, compressing the optic chiasm and cavernous sinuses, and a fluid level on T1 without contrast. Pituitary hormonal assessment showed central hypogonadism, central hypoadrenalism, normal thyroid function, and mildly elevated prolactin. Surgical intervention involved transsphenoidal drainage of a thick-walled abscess, yielding yellowish pus. Histopathological evaluation of the pus suggested an inflammatory lesion, possibly an abscess, with no evidence of pituitary adenoma. Gram stain showed few WBC, but cultures and AFB stain were sterile. Postoperatively, the patient received a 6-week course of metronidazole, ceftriaxone, and vancomycin, leading to improvement in symptoms and normal functional status. Follow-up MRI confirmed complete resolution of abscess pockets.

Intraoperatively, a thick capsule of abscess was incised, and yellowish pus was drained from the pituitary region.
Histopathological evaluation of the drained pus showed features suggestive of an inflammatory lesion, possibly an abscess, with no evidence of pituitary adenoma.
The patient showed clinical improvement in symptoms and achieved normal functional status after surgical drainage and a 6-week course of antibiotics.
Follow-up MRI demonstrated complete resolution of abscess pockets within the pituitary fossa.
